name: Release Management Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in release management work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in release management work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about release management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Keep release management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. Keep release management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. When release management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. When release management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Prefer explicit, readable release management solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. Before starting release management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. When multiple release management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop release management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated release management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of release management correctness.
- Do not apply generic release management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new release management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for release management, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
